title: Lifting a bounded-above projective derived reduction model across a nilpotent ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$, and $C\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $E^\bullet$ be a bounded-above cochain complex of projective $A/I$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Suppose $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I$ is isomorphic in $D(A/I)$ to the image of $E^\bullet$, where derived extension of scalars is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object site with only the identity covering. Then there exists a bounded-above cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules whose image in $D(A)$ is isomorphic to $C$, and whose termwise quotient complex $P^\bullet/IP^\bullet$ is isomorphic to $E^\bullet$ as a complex of $A/I$-modules.

proof.text: Take $\mathcal P$ to be the class of all projective $A$-modules. Using the lifting-along-surjections characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], a map out of $P_1\oplus P_2$ lifts componentwise if both summands are projective; conversely a map out of a summand lifts by precomposing with the projection and restricting a lift. Thus $P_1$ and $P_1\oplus P_2$ belong to $\mathcal P$ if and only if $P_1,P_2$ do. If a module $T$ satisfies $T/IT=0$, then $T=IT=I^2T=\cdots=I^NT=0$. For any map $u$ surjective modulo $I$, its cokernel $T$ satisfies $T/IT=0$: every target element is a sum of an image element and an element of $I$ times the target, so $T=IT$. Hence $u$ is surjective. This verifies hypotheses (1), (2), (3) of the general class lifting theorem without a finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09AR, first three hypotheses of Tag 0BCA; nilpotent Nakayama argument written explicitly

proof.text: For each degree $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-projective-module-lift] to the projective $A/I$-module $E^i$ to choose a projective $A$-module $T_i$ with $T_i/IT_i\cong E^i$. Together with the assumed boundedness above of $E^\bullet$, these are exactly hypothesis (4) of the class lifting theorem. No choice of differentials on the $T_i$ is asserted.

Choose $b\in\mathbf Z$ with $E^i=0$ for $i>b$. The formula $H^i(E)=\ker(d^i)/\operatorname{im}(d^{i-1})$ gives $H^i(E)=0$ in those degrees. The supplied derived isomorphism therefore gives $H^i(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I)=0$ for $i>b$, since cohomology factors through the derived localization. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-derived-upper-bound] to obtain $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 09AR, hypothesis (5), using the upper-bound filtration argument of Tag 0H75

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-above-projective-model] to $C$ and the upper bound just obtained. It gives a complex $L^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules with $L^i=0$ for $i>b$ and $Q(L^\bullet)\cong C$. Thus hypothesis (5) of the general class lifting theorem holds; pseudo-coherence or finite Tor amplitude of $C$ has not been assumed.

Apply [lem-sc-complex-lift-class-projective] with $R=A$, $K=C$, the given ideal $I$, the given complex $E^\bullet$, and the class $\mathcal P$ from step 1. The given derived reduction isomorphism supplies its initial datum; steps 1, 2, 4 verify all five hypotheses. Its conclusion supplies a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules representing $C$ and an isomorphism $P^\bullet/IP^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$ of complexes, precisely both required conclusions.
